You also added three legitimate, well-evidenced findings of your own, the reflected XSS, the SSRF to the metadata service, and the PII exposure, which shows real analytical instinct rather than padding. Where D1 falls short is the entire token and auth-config cluster: the JWT alg:none acceptance, the hardcoded sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 secret, the missing token expiry, and the cookie missing Secure and SameSite flags are all absent, and your decoy section disproves a PHP-session concern you raised yourself rather than the actual planted safe construct, which is the constant-time HS256 verification using hash_equals(). Now the hard part: D2 the exploit chain and CVSS, D3 the client report, and D4 the ethics responses were not in the folder, so each of those three deliverables scored zero, and that is what pulls the overall number down so far despite solid D1 work. Your single most important next step is simply to submit the three missing deliverables, because the skill your D1 already demonstrates tells me you can produce them.
